title: Finite free comparison of the actual quotient Roos complexes before localization
statement: Let R → S be a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on a site essentially small in the module universe, and E its ordinary scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Suppose S is finite free as an R-module, including rank zero. Let t, v and u be global sections with u locally a unit and φ(t)=u v^e for an integer e≥1. Assume countable products of S-module sheaves are exact. Then E is exact. For every cochain complex P the canonical balanced quotient maps give a strict tower isomorphism E(P ⊗ R/t^(n+1)) ≅ (EP ⊗ S/v^(e(n+1)))_n. Its canonical product comparison induces an isomorphism δ between the actual signed Roos cones, with the two specified product coordinates, and arithmetic restriction gives a quasi-isomorphism a with block/selection coordinates. The two cone maps are natural for all cochain maps, and the balanced tower comparison sends the scalar extension of each quotient map to the corresponding target quotient map. All data are packaged in QuotientRoosExchange; no derived completion functor occurs.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YT and 0941; the indicated explicit steps of lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange.

proof.text: Under restriction of scalars, E is tensor with the finite free R-module S. Its finite coordinates identify it naturally with a finite power of the identity. Faithful exact forgetting detects exactness and the invertibility of the canonical product comparison.

The equality φ(t)^n=u^n v^(en) identifies the quotient ideals. The balanced local tensor maps and their inverses on local quotient lifts give β. Changing a lift by v^(en) changes the tensor by zero. Check restrictions, chain differentials, transitions, quotient augmentations and input chain maps on local tensor generators.

Apply the additive Roos comparison to E and β. Its product projections and cone coordinates are the required formulas for c and δ. The arithmetic selection/block square yields a, which is a quasi-isomorphism by arithmetic restriction and exact products. Every construction is natural for strict chain maps.

proof_origin.place: Explicit refinement of the balanced quotient and resolving-class arguments in lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange.

theorem finiteFreeQuotientRoosComparison
    (F : SheafOfModules.DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel.{u, v, r, wR, wS} φ)
    (hfree : ∃ d : ℕ, Nonempty
      ((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).map φ)).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)) ≅
        ∐ (fun _ : Fin d ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
          (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R))))
    (t : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J R)).sections)
    (vS : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)).sections)
    (uS : (SheafOfModules.unit
      (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S)).sections)
    (hu : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ, IsUnit (@id (S.obj.obj U) (uS.val U)))
    (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e)
    (hrelation : ∀ U : Cᵒᵖ,
      φ.hom.app U (@id (R.obj.obj U) (t.val U)) =
        (@id (S.obj.obj U) (uS.val U)) * (@id (S.obj.obj U) (vS.val U)) ^ e)
    [HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ)
      (ringedSiteModules.{r} (SheafOfModules.derivedChangeRingIndependentCoefficients J S))] :
    Nonempty (QuotientRoosExchange F t vS e)
